evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor drops from 12.25 mg/L at 46.0 h to 3.69 mg/L at 46.2 h
DO2 reaches 1.73 mg/L at 52.0 h, below the 2.0 mg/L minimum constraint
All three source batches maintained DO2 >= 7.4 mg/L through 96 h, indicating a receiving-specific oxygen supply/demand mismatch
Receiving P assay: 0.90 g/L at 36 h and 2.33 g/L at 48 h (vs ~3.0 g/L in sources), showing active but constrained production at decision time
allowed_actions: increase_air bounded [1.0, 1.15]; reduce_feed/combined would cut feed and risk product mass; stop yields zero production
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~46 h (12.2 -> 3.7 mg/L) and fell below the 2.0 mg/L minimum (1.73 mg/L at t=52 h), unlike any source batch, indicating a receiving-specific oxygen supply deficit with active production (P rising: 0.90 g/L at 36 h, 2.33 g/L at 48 h). increase_air raises aeration up to 1.15x to restore DO2 above the constraint while leaving feed untouched, preserving product mass; feed reductions or stop would sacrifice titer, and waiting for an extra assay under KEEP would deepen the violation.
args.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters make the required aeration gain uncertain; 1.15x may be insufficient if oxygen demand keeps growing, in which case a follow-up combined action may be needed. Current P is estimated from a 4h-delayed assay; exact titer at decision time is unknown. No physics tool was available to pre-validate the 1.15x effect.
